acceptance: nightly-v2 validated by 2-3 workflow_dispatch runs (off-peak where possible) with a job-level comparison to the old nightly/scheduled workflows' latest results; no 7-night shadow
Each domain has its own job conclusion, artifacts, and label; t3:cloud gated off by repo variable
Durations file refreshed by the run
macOS/Windows wheel install and Python 3.11-3.14 matrix included (moved out of T2)
Owner response policy documented: fix or revert within one working day
context: Moved before any deletion per codex C6 / agy A5 / muse M11. Guardrails G2, G3. Owner decision: t3:cloud is wired but gated by a repo variable (e.g. BENCHBOX_T3_CLOUD_ENABLED) that defaults to off; the agent never runs live cloud tests. Parity for the cloud domain is by static comparison with the old nightly jobs, not execution.
description: New .github/workflows/nightly-v2.yml (renamed to nightly.yml when the old one retires in dlv2-70) at trunk tip with separate jobs and separate failure labels: t3:docker (postgres, clickhouse, trino from docker-integration.yml), t3:cloud (credentialed, optional), t3:perf (perf-smoke), t3:matrix (Python 3.11-3.14 x Linux/macOS/Windows from cross-platform-validation.yml), t3:browser (firefox/webkit explorer), t3:extension (duckdb-datasketches from extension-smoke.yml), t3:install (pypi-latest installability from release-canary.yml), t3:drift (weekly: corpus-drift, pricing-data drift, submission-validator drift, cross-surface baseline autodetect); plus quarantined tests and durations-file refresh. Each failing domain opens/updates one issue with its own label and owner. An open t3:* issue marked release-blocking blocks release.yml (dlv2-51). The trunk-tip run replaces the develop-post-merge push-triggered re-run.
